root: repo - Tool-neutral build entry with two implementations: Nx with Bun (default) and Bazel.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel] <command> [options] [-- <arguments>]
repo <command> --help [--lang=en|de]
Commands:
run <project:target[:configuration]>            Run one task of one project.
run-many --targets=<targets> [--projects=<projects>]
Run the same targets in many projects.
affected --targets=<targets>                    Run targets in the projects changed against HEAD and their dependents.
exec --projects=<projects> -- <command>         Run a command once per selected project, in the project root.
watch --projects=<projects> -- <command>        Rerun a command when selected source files change.
graph                                           Print the tool-neutral build graph.
show projects|project <name>|targets            Print projects, one project or all targets of the neutral graph.
inputs <project:target[:configuration]>         Print what the selected implementation hashes for one task: files, environment, runtime values and external packages.
reset                                           Invalidate the graph and reset the selected tool's local state.
tools setup [nx|bazel|all]                      Provision the pinned build tools for this host.
preflight                                       Check the host against the finite requirements before any store is provisioned.
incremental list|plan|prepare|run|discard       Prove in a disposable copy that Nx and Bazel rebuild exactly what an edit affects, no more and no less.

concurrency list|plan|run                       Prove that simulated agents working in one checkout copy at the same time never wait for unrelated projects, share cached work and get the results of a serial run, with Nx and Bazel.
dependencies sync|lock --all|--scope <owner> | ensure
Install, lock or ensure the workspace dependencies.
cargo --store=shared|isolated --configuration=prototype|release [--parallelism=<cores>] -- <cargo subcommand> <args>
Compile through the repository's Cargo ingress gate.

cache status|gc|clear|remote status|serve       Show and collect every declared cache home with its budget, clear the selected tool's local task cache, show the remote cache contract, or serve a remote cache.
capacity status|run                             Show the machine's free memory, floor, load and the running and waiting grants, or run any command under a machine-wide capacity grant.

leases status                                   Show which processes hold and wait for resource leases, how long, who blocks whom, deadlock cycles, lock order violations and the machine's admission queue.
remote-execution serve|status|env               Run, inspect or describe the optional local remote execution cluster that hermetic Bazel actions can run on.
Options:
-p, --projects=<projects>                       Comma list of project names with * wildcards, tag:<tag>, name:<name>, directory:<root> and !<pattern> negation. (used by: run-many, exec, watch)
--exclude=<projects>                            Comma list of projects to leave out (same patterns as --projects). (used by: run-many, affected, exec, watch)
-t, --targets=<targets>, --target               Comma list of target names or * patterns. (used by: run-many, affected)

-c, --configuration=<prototype|release>         Compiler configuration; disagreeing values (also a :<configuration> suffix or SEMIO_BUILD_MODE) are refused; cargo takes the full name only. (used by: run, run-many, affected, cargo)
--parallel=<n>                                  Maximum number of concurrent tasks. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--bail                                          Stop at the first failing task. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--verbose                                       Print more detail. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--output=<stream|stream-without-prefixes|static>, --output-style
Output style of the task logs. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--skip-cache                                    Ignore the task cache. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--skip-remote-cache                             Ignore the remote cache. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--exclude-dependencies, --exclude-task-dependencies
Run only the named tasks, not the tasks they depend on. (used by: run, run-many, affected)

--dry-run                                       Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing. (used by: run, run-many, affected, exec, cache)

--graph[=<file>]                                Same as --dry-run; with a file the plan is written there (Nx: the file as given, Bazel: a report whose path is printed). (used by: run, run-many, affected, exec)

--all                                           Select every project (affected, watch), every dependency owner (dependencies) or every lease directory with registered processes (leases). (used by: affected, watch, dependencies, leases)
--base=<ref>                                    Compare against this revision instead of HEAD. (used by: affected)
--head=<ref>                                    End revision of the comparison. (used by: affected)
--files=<files>                                 Comma list of changed files instead of the git comparison. (used by: affected)
--uncommitted                                   Only uncommitted changes. (used by: affected)
--untracked                                     Only untracked files. (used by: affected)
--include-global-files                          Also react to files outside any project. (used by: watch)
--file=<path>                                   Write the result as a report file and print its path. (used by: graph, show, incremental, concurrency)
--json                                          Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line. (used by: graph, show, incremental, concurrency, capacity, leases, cache)
--area=<id[,id]>                                cache status|gc: limit the report or the collection to these ledger areas (or retired, undeclared). (used by: cache)
--tasks                                         cache status: print the selected tool's task cache (a CacheStatus) instead of the cache ledger. (used by: cache)

--implementations=<nx,bazel>                    incremental and concurrency plan|run: implementations to judge (default: both). (used by: incremental, concurrency)

--workloads=<ids|all>                           concurrency plan|run: comma list of workload ids, or all. (used by: concurrency)

--criteria=<id>                                 concurrency run: judge every workload with this set of pass criteria instead of its own. (used by: concurrency)

--store=<shared|isolated>                       Cargo target store; never create a private target directory. (used by: cargo)

Build what differs between two revisions.
Notes:
- Changed files: tracked changes against HEAD plus untracked files by default; --base/--head, --files, --uncommitted and --untracked narrow them; --all selects every project.

- Nx translation: no selector adds --base=HEAD, --uncommitted with --untracked becomes --base=HEAD, --all becomes run-many. The project closure stays tool-native (the Nx project graph; for Bazel a reverse-dependency query over a generated package of project and changed-file nodes, which asserts the same answer).

- Affected projects (identical for every tool, asserted against Nx's own locators): the deepest project root that owns a changed file, projects whose target inputs name a changed {workspaceRoot}/ file, every project when nx.json changes, then all dependents. Package manager manifest and lock semantics (Nx diffs package.json) are Nx-only.
- --projects is refused for every tool; use run-many to narrow.

--json               Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.
--dry-run            Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing.

Global options:

Examples:

Show every cache partition and area against its budget.

List what the collector would remove.

Show the Bazel disk cache and build activity.

Empty the Nx task cache.
repo cache serve
Serve a local remote cache on 127.0.0.1:6090.
repo cache remote status --tool=bazel
Show how Bazel uses the remote cache and whether it answers.
Notes:
- undefined
- undefined
- Nx: status walks the artifacts directory of the Nx cache partition, clear resets only the Nx task cache inside the bounded Nx namespace.

- Bazel: status counts the files of the disk cache entry folders (action cache and content-addressed store) of the products partition and adds the recorded build activity (builds, actions, executed, cacheHits) read from the build event stream; clear stops the persistent servers, removes their output bases (the local action cache) and empties the disk cache, so the next build is a miss; toolchains and modules stay.

- The remote cache is off until SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_ENDPOINT names an http or https origin. SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_INSTANCE, _ACCESS (read-only|read-write), _UPLOAD, _COMPRESSION, _DOWNLOAD (toplevel|all), _TIMEOUT_SECONDS and _RETRIES override the defaults of the build policy; the access token is read from the variable named by SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_TOKEN_ENVIRONMENT (default SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_TOKEN) and is never written to disk.

- Bazel renders the contract into its remote cache settings (endpoint, instance name, upload, compression, download mode, timeout, retries) and passes the token through a credential helper. Nx renders it into its self-hosted remote cache variables (server and access token); it cannot honour compression, download mode, timeouts or retries and leaves read-only to the scope of the server's token. remote status prints both facts.

- serve speaks the HTTP cache protocol of Bazel (GET, HEAD and PUT on /ac/<sha256> and /cas/<sha256>, blobs verified against their digest) and the self-hosted cache API of Nx (GET and PUT on /v1/cache/<hash>, 409 when an entry exists), each under an optional /<instance> prefix. Bearer tokens come from SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER_READ_TOKEN and SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER_WRITE_TOKEN; without a token it refuses to listen beyond loopback. The store is bounded and evicts the least recently used entries; serve publishes progress while it scans the store and stops at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels.

remote-execution: repo remote-execution - Startet, prüft oder beschreibt den optionalen lokalen Remote-Execution-Cluster, auf dem hermetische Bazel-Actions laufen können.
Verwendung:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel] remote-execution serve|status|env [optionen]
Unterbefehle:
remote-execution serve   Betreibt den lokalen Cluster (Speicher, Frontend, Scheduler, Worker, Runner) in Containern bis zum Stopp und entfernt danach Container und Volumes.
remote-execution status  Gibt einen RemoteExecutionServiceStatus aus: ob die Container-Laufzeit antwortet, die Container des Clusters und ob das Frontend antwortet.
remote-execution env     Gibt die Vertragsvariablen aus, die ein Client für den Cluster setzt, je Zeile NAME=Wert.
Optionen:
--platform <linux-arm64|linux-x64>  remote-execution: Ausführungsplattform der Worker; sonst die zur CPU dieses Rechners passende.

--port <port>                       cache serve: Port, auf dem gelauscht wird; 0 wählt einen freien Port (Standard aus der Build-Policy). remote-execution: Loopback-Port des Cluster-Frontends (Standard 8980).
--diagnostics-port <port>           remote-execution: Loopback-Port der Gesundheitsroute des Frontends (Standard 8981).
Globale Optionen:
--tool=<nx|bazel>   Wählt die Build-Implementierung; sonst SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, dann der Standard der Policy (nx).
--workers=<on|off>  Führt Aktionen in persistenten Workern (on) oder je in einem eigenen Prozess (off) aus; sonst SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, dann die Worker-Policy der Build-Policy.
-h, --help          Gibt die Verwendung des Befehls aus und endet.

--lang=<en|de>      Sprache der Texte; sonst SEMIO_LANGUAGE, dann LANGUAGE und die Locale-Variablen (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), dann die Sprache des Betriebssystems. Es wird keine Sprache angenommen: Der Befehl verweigert sich, wenn keine bestimmt werden kann.
Beispiele:
repo remote-execution serve
Betreibt den lokalen Cluster auf 127.0.0.1:8980 mit Workern passend zur CPU dieses Rechners.
repo remote-execution env --platform=linux-x64
Gibt die Variablen aus, die hermetische Actions an x64-Linux-Worker leiten.
repo remote-execution status
Zeigt Laufzeit, Container und ob das Frontend antwortet.
Hinweise:

- Optionaler Entwicklerdienst, nie eine Abhängigkeit: Ist SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_ENDPOINT nicht gesetzt, bleibt jede Aktion lokal. Dienstbeschreibung, Schema und festgelegte Container-Images liegen im Build-Modul; jedes Image ist ein offizielles und per Digest festgelegt.

- serve braucht eine laufende Container-Runtime (Docker Desktop oder der docker-Dienst) und das Compose-Plugin. Es kopiert den paketierten Stack in ein ASCII-only Laufzeitverzeichnis unterhalb des Workspace, startet den Cluster nur auf Loopback (der Cluster hat keine Authentifizierung), gibt die Client-Variablen aus, sobald das Frontend antwortet, und entfernt bei Abbruch Container und Volumes: Sein Zustand ist flüchtig und lokal auf dieser Maschine.

- Die Worker melden die Eigenschaften ihrer Ausführungsplattform (linux-arm64 oder linux-x64) und den Instanznamen main; die ausgegebenen Variablen setzen, danach hermetische Targets mit der Bazel-Implementierung ausführen.
- serve meldet Fortschritt beim Prüfen der Runtime, Erzeugen des Stacks, Starten des Clusters und Abbauen; status und env ändern nichts.
